content.title: About
content.content: Swiss cheese is a semi‑hard cheese with characteristic holes, made from cow’s milk. It has a mild nutty flavor and a slightly sweet aroma. Traditional aging ranges from 3 to 12 months, during which the iconic “eyes” develop.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Swiss cheese is best known under the brand name “Emmental,” though Switzerland produces many regional varieties.
The holes are created by Propionibacterium freudenreichii bacteria, which release carbon dioxide.
It is a key ingredient in fondue, a classic Swiss melted‑cheese dish.
In the United States the cheese is simply called “Swiss cheese,” while in Switzerland it has different regional names.
When aged up to 24 months, the flavor becomes more intense and aromatic.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium supports strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which aid nerve function and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic bacteria
items.content: The bacteria used in ripening may benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: During aging much of the lactose is broken down, making it more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to Swiss cheese.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese is salty, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of its fat content, it is calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Excess saturated fat may raise cholesterol levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Swiss cheese is great sliced for sandwiches, added to salads, grated over pasta and casseroles, melted in fondue, baked in gratins, or used as a filling for omelets.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in the refrigerator wrapped in wax paper or parchment, then placed in a plastic container. Properly stored, it keeps its flavor for 4‑6 weeks. Discard if any non‑white mold appears.
